item.content:encoded:
The Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL) is opening its 2026–2027 recruitment cycle, providing an opportunity for qualified candidates interested in research, data, fieldwork, development economics, public policy, and evidence-based approaches to poverty reduction to apply for positions across its global network.

The recruitment drive is particularly relevant for candidates seeking to build careers in international development research and work alongside researchers, academic institutions, and organizations conducting rigorous evaluations of policies and programs designed to improve people’s lives.

J-PAL and professors at affiliated research institutions around the world are accepting applications for General Data Research Associate and General Field Research Associate positions during the early phase of the recruitment cycle. The wider recruitment drive will subsequently open applications for additional positions.

About J-PAL

The Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL) is a global research network that works with researchers and policymakers to generate evidence and translate research into policy and practice.

Its work focuses on using rigorous research and data to understand which approaches can effectively address challenges associated with poverty and social and economic development.

J-PAL works through a network of affiliated researchers, regional offices, academic institutions, governments, and partner organizations around the world. This makes its recruitment opportunities particularly valuable for individuals who want to gain experience in international development, empirical research, policy evaluation, data analysis, and field-based research.

Working within the J-PAL network can also provide exposure to multidisciplinary research projects and collaboration with researchers and organizations operating in different countries and sectors.

J-PAL 2026–2027 Recruitment Drive

J-PAL conducts recruitment throughout the year, but a substantial number of positions are filled during its annual recruitment drives.

The annual recruitment drive is therefore an important period for people seeking employment with J-PAL and its affiliated organizations. Applying during the recruitment drive can increase the likelihood that an application will be considered by multiple researchers and hiring managers within the network.

For the 2026–2027 recruitment cycle, J-PAL has introduced an early launch for two major categories of research positions:

  • General Data Research Associate
  • General Field Research Associate

The early recruitment period runs from September 8, 2026, through October 9, 2026.

The full recruitment drive will then open on November 25, 2026, with applications remaining open until January 13, 2027.

Key Recruitment Dates

  • Early launch: September 8, 2026
  • Early launch closes: October 9, 2026
  • Full recruitment drive opens: November 25, 2026
  • Final application deadline: January 13, 2027
  • Expected interview period: From the end of January through spring 2027
  • Typical start period: Many positions begin around June, although start dates vary by position and organization

Applicants interested in the General Data Research Associate or General Field Research Associate opportunities should therefore pay particular attention to the early application period rather than waiting until the full recruitment drive opens.

General Data Research Associate Positions

The General Data Research Associate recruitment track is intended for candidates interested in research work involving data, quantitative analysis, research implementation, and evidence generation.

Data Research Associates can work on projects where researchers use data to evaluate development programs, public policies, and interventions.

Depending on the specific position and research project, the work may involve activities such as:

  • Collecting and managing research data
  • Cleaning and organizing datasets
  • Conducting quantitative analysis
  • Supporting research design and implementation
  • Assisting researchers with empirical research
  • Preparing research materials and documentation
  • Working with statistical or analytical tools
  • Contributing to research outputs
  • Supporting rigorous impact evaluations
  • Helping transform research findings into evidence that can inform policy

Candidates interested in economics, statistics, data science, public policy, social sciences, development studies, and related fields may find this recruitment track particularly relevant.

General Field Research Associate Positions

The General Field Research Associate track is focused more directly on implementing and supporting research activities in the field.

Field-based research is an important component of many J-PAL projects because rigorous evaluations frequently require researchers and research teams to work directly with communities, institutions, governments, businesses, or other stakeholders.

Depending on the particular project, field research responsibilities may include:

  • Supporting field research operations
  • Coordinating research activities
  • Assisting with data collection
  • Working with local research teams
  • Supporting surveys and field experiments
  • Coordinating with project stakeholders
  • Monitoring field activities
  • Helping ensure that research protocols are followed
  • Supporting the implementation of impact evaluations
  • Contributing to the accurate collection and management of research information

Field research positions may be especially attractive to candidates who enjoy practical, project-based work and are interested in understanding how development programs operate in real-world settings.

Who Can Apply?

The recruitment drive is intended for qualified candidates interested in research and development-related employment opportunities within the J-PAL network and its affiliated research institutions and organizations.

Applicants should carefully review the requirements of each individual position because eligibility, academic qualifications, technical skills, language requirements, geographic requirements, and other selection criteria can differ between jobs.

The General Data Research Associate and General Field Research Associate positions are particularly relevant to candidates with backgrounds or interests in areas such as:

  • Economics
  • Development economics
  • Statistics
  • Data science
  • Econometrics
  • Public policy
  • Political science
  • International development
  • Social sciences
  • Research methods
  • Quantitative research
  • Other related academic and professional disciplines

Candidates should not assume that every J-PAL position has identical requirements. The appropriate qualifications will depend on the particular researcher, project, institution, location, and position.

Geographic Eligibility

J-PAL is a global research network, with affiliated researchers and partner organizations located in different parts of the world.

The recruitment information indicates that hiring managers may consider applicants based on factors including geographic location, alongside the strength of their applications, flexibility, and language skills.

This means applicants from different countries and regions may be considered where their qualifications and circumstances align with available positions.

Importantly, the recruitment information does not establish a blanket race- or continent-specific restriction for the overall recruitment drive. Applicants should instead examine the eligibility requirements of the specific job they wish to pursue, as some positions may have location-specific or language-related requirements.

Candidates from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, Latin America and the Caribbean, the Middle East, Oceania, and other regions may potentially find relevant opportunities within the broader J-PAL network, subject to the requirements of individual vacancies.

How the J-PAL Recruitment Drive Works

J-PAL’s recruitment process allows researchers and affiliated organizations to identify candidates for research positions through the network’s recruitment system.

During the annual recruitment drive, J-PAL publicizes available opportunities and solicits applications from candidates interested in joining its research network.

Applicants submit a Common Application, selecting the jobs for which they are interested and qualified.

The application process is designed to make it easier for researchers and affiliated organizations within the network to identify suitable candidates.

What Happens After You Apply?

After applications are submitted, J-PAL staff, researchers, and hiring managers may review candidates based on several considerations.

According to the recruitment information, these include:

  1. Strength of the application
    The quality and relevance of a candidate’s academic background, professional experience, skills, and application materials can influence their prospects.
  2. Geographic location
    Some research projects require candidates to be located in particular countries or regions, making geographic considerations relevant to recruitment.
  3. Flexibility
    Candidates’ flexibility may be considered depending on the needs of the position and research project.
  4. Language skills
    Language capabilities can be important, particularly for field research and projects involving local communities or institutions.

Candidates who are shortlisted may be contacted for interviews.

J-PAL Interview and Selection Timeline

Shortlisted candidates may begin receiving interview invitations from the end of January through spring 2027.

One notable feature of the J-PAL recruitment process is that candidates may receive interviews from several researchers or organizations during the selection process.

This means a candidate’s application may potentially attract interest from more than one research team or affiliated organization.

Candidates should therefore ensure that their applications clearly communicate their qualifications, technical abilities, research interests, geographic flexibility, language capabilities, and relevant experience.

Potential Start Dates

Start dates vary depending on the position, research project, and employing organization.

However, J-PAL indicates that many positions have start dates in June.

Applicants should therefore carefully check the start date associated with individual positions when considering opportunities available through the recruitment drive.

A candidate who is successful in the recruitment process may need to make arrangements around employment transition, relocation, academic commitments, or other responsibilities depending on the position.

J-PAL Common Application

A central component of the recruitment drive is the Common Application.

Candidates interested in participating in the drive should submit the Common Application and select the positions they are interested in and qualified for.

Applicants should avoid selecting positions simply because they are available. Instead, they should identify opportunities where their academic qualifications, professional experience, technical abilities, research interests, language skills, and geographic circumstances closely match the requirements.

This approach can help candidates present a more targeted and credible application.

APPLY HERE

Other Organizations in the J-PAL Recruitment Network

The recruitment drive is not limited exclusively to positions directly employed by J-PAL.

Organizations affiliated with J-PAL, as well as researchers and organizations associated with other major research networks, may participate in recruitment.

The recruitment information specifically notes that organizations affiliated with J-PAL, IPA, EPoD, and CEGA may choose to post jobs on the Common Application.

This makes the recruitment platform a potentially valuable resource for candidates seeking research positions beyond a single institution.

Rolling Recruitment Outside the Annual Drive

Candidates should also understand that they do not necessarily have to wait for the annual recruitment drive to find opportunities.

J-PAL conducts rolling recruitment throughout the year, with positions recruited individually according to the needs of specific projects.

For these positions, recruitment timelines depend on the project and employing organization.

Individual vacancies may include:

  • A proposed start date
  • A specific application deadline
  • Position-specific eligibility requirements
  • Project-specific qualifications
  • Geographic requirements
  • Language requirements
  • Other selection criteria

Because rolling recruitment operates independently of the annual recruitment drive, candidates should regularly monitor J-PAL’s careers opportunities.

Why Applicants Should Apply Early

J-PAL recommends applying as soon as possible, particularly for positions recruited outside the main annual drive.

For specifically posted positions, the majority of finalists are generally contacted by hiring managers within a month of applying.

For the annual recruitment drive, early application is also strategically important because applicants may be reviewed by multiple researchers and hiring managers across the network.

Candidates should therefore avoid waiting until the final day of the application period if they already have the necessary information and documents prepared.

How to Strengthen Your J-PAL Application

Competition for international development research positions can be significant. Candidates can improve their applications by ensuring that they demonstrate a clear connection between their background and the requirements of the positions they select.

1. Match Your Background to the Position

Before applying, carefully examine the responsibilities and requirements of each job.

Your application should demonstrate how your education, research experience, analytical skills, professional experience, and other competencies relate directly to the position.

2. Highlight Quantitative and Research Skills

For Data Research Associate positions, candidates should clearly present relevant experience with:

  • Data analysis
  • Statistical analysis
  • Econometrics
  • Research methodology
  • Data management
  • Statistical software
  • Programming or data science, where applicable
  • Quantitative research

Where possible, applicants should demonstrate how they have used these skills in actual projects rather than simply listing them.

3. Demonstrate Field Research Experience

Candidates applying for Field Research Associate opportunities should highlight experience involving:

  • Fieldwork
  • Surveys
  • Data collection
  • Community engagement
  • Research implementation
  • Project coordination
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • Monitoring research activities

Relevant experience does not necessarily have to come from a job specifically titled “Field Research Associate.” Academic research, internships, development projects, and other practical research experiences may be relevant where they demonstrate transferable skills.

4. Highlight Language Skills

Language ability can be important for research conducted in different countries and communities.

Applicants should clearly identify languages they speak and their proficiency levels where relevant to the position.

5. Demonstrate Flexibility

Because J-PAL works across different countries, projects, and research environments, flexibility can be an important consideration.

Applicants should clearly communicate relevant geographic, professional, or project flexibility when appropriate.

6. Prepare for Multiple Interviews

Because candidates may potentially be contacted by several researchers or organizations during the recruitment process, applicants should be prepared to discuss their experience and suitability for different research projects.

A strong candidate should be able to clearly explain:

  • Why they are interested in J-PAL
  • Their research interests
  • Their relevant academic background
  • Their technical skills
  • Their field or project experience
  • Their career goals
  • Their interest in evidence-based policy
  • Why their skills are relevant to the particular research project

Important Dates at a Glance

Recruitment Stage Date
Early launch for General Data Research Associate and General Field Research Associate September 8, 2026
Early application period closes October 9, 2026
Full recruitment drive opens November 25, 2026
Final application deadline January 13, 2027
Expected interviews End of January through spring 2027
Many anticipated position start dates June 2027

Applicants should verify the details of individual vacancies because position-specific requirements and deadlines may differ.

Visit HERE for more information about the J-PAL 2026–2027 Recruitment Drive.

Conclusion

The J-PAL 2026–2027 Recruitment Drive presents an important employment opportunity for candidates seeking careers in international development, research, data analysis, field research, economics, public policy, and evidence-based policymaking.

The recruitment process is particularly significant because applicants are not necessarily applying to a single research team. Through the J-PAL network and Common Application, candidates may be considered by multiple researchers and affiliated organizations looking for research talent.

The early recruitment period for General Data Research Associate and General Field Research Associate positions runs from September 8 to October 9, 2026, while the full recruitment drive opens on November 25, 2026, and closes on January 13, 2027.

Candidates interested in these opportunities should begin preparing their applications early, carefully select positions for which they are qualified, and ensure that their academic background, research experience, technical capabilities, language skills, geographic circumstances, and career interests are clearly presented.

For aspiring researchers and development professionals, joining J-PAL or one of its affiliated research organizations can provide valuable exposure to rigorous research, international development projects, data-driven policymaking, and collaboration with researchers working to generate evidence on some of the world’s most important social and economic challenges.

WMO Internships

Key Details

Opportunity WMO Internship Programme
Organisation World Meteorological Organization (WMO)
Who can apply? Students and recent graduates worldwide
Age 21–35 years for recent graduates
Work experience Less than 2 years of relevant experience
Fields Meteorology, climatology, hydrology, geophysical sciences, international administration and related areas
Language English required; UN languages desirable
Duration 3–12 months
Stipend – Geneva CHF 1,500/month
Stipend – Remote CHF 300/month
Application Online
Deadline Varies by internship opening
Location Geneva, WMO Regional/Sub-Regional Offices and remote
WMO is looking for talented, motivated, and passionate interns from around the world who want to bring their innovative ideas, unique experiences, and personal curiosity to our organization.

The WMO Internship Programme offers students and recent graduates a wide range of opportunities and experience in various fields and activities to help forge a foundation for their future careers.

Interns work in a number of fields, spanning meteorology, climatology, operational hydrology and related geophysical sciences, as well as in public international administration.

The Internship Programme has agreements with universities and academic institutions specializing in areas relevant to WMO activities and Programmes. This collaboration contributes to the mutual exchange of knowledge and expertise.

Am I eligible for an internship?

The WMO Internship Programme is open to all students and recent graduates who:

  • Are interested in an area related to WMO’s core activities
  • Are students approaching the end of their studies and preparing a thesis
  • Are students who need an internship to complete their studies
  • Have recently graduated and are between the age of 21 and 35 years old
  • Have less than two years of relevant work experience
  • Hold a scholarship for an internship placement in an international organization
  • Are sponsored by a governmental/non-governmental entity such as an NGO
  • Are sponsored by academic institutions to work in specific areas within WMO

View current openings

WMO e-Recruitment site

What skills should I have?

You will need to be able to adapt to an international, multicultural and multilingual environment. You must have good communication skills and be able to work effectively within a team.

Working knowledge of English (both oral and written) is essential. Knowledge of a second UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish) is desirable.

What learning elements you will take from the internship?

Understanding of WMO’s mandate and related knowledge and skills.

Comprehend applicable WMO related rules, guidance, etc, and a general understanding of WMO and UN work processes and policies.

Complete WMO related mandatory trainings.

Carry out the supporting function processes in related department and understand the challenges and opportunities in a multicultural environment of an international intergovernmental specialized agency in the UN system.

Strengthen professional oral and written communication skills.

Develop and maintain relations with various stakeholders and develop networks with considerable insight into the real practice within the WMO and UN system.

Frequently asked questions

Stipend

  • Interns recruited in Geneva will receive a stipend of CHF 1 500 per month.
  • Interns recruited to serve in the WMO Regional/Sub-Regional Offices will receive a 10% Daily Subsistence Allowance (DSA) for 30 days per month.
  • Interns who are working remotely will receive a stipend of CHF 300 per month.
  • If funded by a Member State or university, the allowance rate follows the policy of the sending entity.

Duration

  • Interns are employed for a minimum of three months to a maximum of twelve months.

Annual Leave

  • Interns earn 2.5 days of leave per month through the duration of their internship
  • Any unused annual leave is not compensated at the end of the internship.

Insurance

  • All interns based outside of Switzerland are covered by CIGNA Insurance for Sickness and Accidents. CIGNA enrollment and fees are covered by WMO.
  • For all interns based in Switzerland, health and accident insurance is mandatory. Interns are recommended to subscribe to Swisscare for Sickness and Accident insurance. Enrollment in the insurance plan is done by the Intern. WMO covers the expense by adding the insurance cost to the Intern’s monthly stipend.
  • Locally recruited interns who are already insured under another policy can opt-out of being covered by Swisscare.
  • Interns based in all WMO duty stations are covered by the WMO Benefits insurance Plan and the WMO Malicious Act Insurance Policy (MAIP).
  • In the exceptional event that an intern is requested to travel for work, they will be covered by Accident and Illness insurance.

item.content:encoded:
Manav Rachna University (MUJ) has launched its Post-Doctoral Fellowship (PDF) program to encourage theoretical and conceptual advancements across disciplines while attracting promising young research talent from around the world. The program is designed to support outstanding scholars from India and abroad who have demonstrated strong academic and research achievements and are ready to undertake advanced post-doctoral research.

The MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship provides financial support through a monthly stipend of ₹70,000, along with two annual contingency grants worth ₹50,000 each. Together, these provisions are intended to support researchers with living costs, professional conferences, presentations, publication expenses, research consumables and necessary equipment.

The fellowship is particularly competitive because applicants must already hold a PhD, be under 35 years of age, and have published at least four papers in Q1/Q2 journals within the previous two years.

MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship Overview

The MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship has been established to strengthen research and encourage young scholars to contribute to theoretical and conceptual developments in different academic disciplines.

The program is open to scholars from all nationalities, making it an international post-doctoral research opportunity. Applicants are expected to demonstrate strong research credentials and a recent publication record before they can be considered.

The fellowship initially lasts for one year, with the possibility of an additional year depending on satisfactory research performance and progress.

Key features include:

  • Monthly stipend of ₹70,000
  • Annual Contingency Grant – Part I of ₹50,000
  • Annual Contingency Grant – Part II of ₹50,000
  • Fellowship initially awarded for one year
  • Possibility of a one-year extension
  • Applications invited throughout the year
  • Monthly interviews for shortlisted candidates, subject to expert panel availability
  • Dedicated supervision and research-progress monitoring
  • Opportunity to undertake academic responsibilities related to teaching and learning
  • International eligibility with applicants from all nationalities welcome

MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship Financial Benefits

One of the major attractions of the MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship is the financial package provided to successful fellows.

1. Monthly Stipend of ₹70,000

Selected Post-Doctoral Fellows will receive a monthly stipend of ₹70,000.

This financial support is intended to provide fellows with regular funding throughout the fellowship and enable them to focus on their research activities.

Over an initial 12-month fellowship period, the monthly stipend amounts to ₹840,000, before considering the additional contingency grants.

2. Contingency Grant – Part I: ₹50,000 Per Year

MUJ provides an annual ₹50,000 Contingency Grant – Part I.

According to the fellowship guidelines, this funding can be used for research-related professional activities such as:

  • Attending professional conferences
  • Presenting research at conferences
  • Covering publication charges

This component can therefore help fellows participate in academic activities beyond their immediate research environment and disseminate their findings through professional and scholarly channels.

3. Contingency Grant – Part II: ₹50,000 Per Year

Fellows will also receive a ₹50,000 annual Contingency Grant – Part II.

This component is intended for research-related requirements, including:

  • Procurement of consumables
  • Necessary equipment

The two contingency grants provide a combined annual allocation of ₹100,000, in addition to the monthly stipend.

Who Is Eligible for the MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship?

The MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship has specific eligibility conditions that applicants must satisfy.

Candidates should carefully review each requirement before applying because the fellowship is intended for young researchers who have already demonstrated substantial research achievement.

1. Open to All Nationalities

The fellowship is open to applicants of all nationalities.

This means the opportunity is not restricted to Indian citizens. Scholars from other countries are also eligible to apply, provided they meet the academic, age, publication and other fellowship requirements.

2. Age Requirement

Applicants must be under 35 years of age at the time of application submission.

The age requirement is therefore assessed at the point when the application is submitted.

3. PhD Requirement

Applicants must hold a PhD from a recognized institute in India or abroad.

This means that the fellowship is specifically designed for researchers who have already completed doctoral-level study and are seeking to continue developing their research careers through post-doctoral work.

4. Additional Requirement for MUJ PhD Graduates

Candidates who completed their PhD at MUJ must have at least one year of post-PhD experience in a relevant field outside MUJ.

This requirement specifically applies to candidates whose doctoral degree was completed at MUJ.

5. Publication Requirement

Applicants must have published at least four papers in Q1/Q2 quartile journals during the last two years.

This is one of the fellowship’s most significant research requirements.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate a recent and substantial publication record rather than relying solely on publications from earlier stages of their academic careers.

6. No Other External Financial Support

Applicants must not be receiving another form of:

  • External grant
  • Financial aid
  • Research assistance

during the fellowship.

Candidates who are already receiving external research funding or financial assistance should carefully consider this condition before applying.

7. No Other Employment During the Fellowship

Selected fellows must not undertake part-time or full-time employment, whether remunerative or honorary, for the entire duration of the fellowship.

The fellowship therefore requires the fellow to comply with the employment restriction throughout the fellowship period.

Duration of the MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship

The MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship is initially awarded for one year.

However, fellows may have the opportunity to continue for another year if their performance and research progress are considered satisfactory.

The possible extension is not automatic. Research performance and progress will be reviewed by a committee before an additional year can be granted.

This structure provides researchers with the possibility of undertaking a longer post-doctoral research program while maintaining a formal performance-review process.

Academic Responsibilities During the Fellowship

Although the primary purpose of the fellowship is research, fellows may also be assigned academic responsibilities related to teaching and learning.

Such responsibilities may be allocated within the relevant department according to its requirements.

Prospective applicants should therefore understand that the fellowship may involve both research activities and certain academic responsibilities, depending on departmental needs.

MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship Application and Recruitment Process

MUJ invites applications from eligible candidates throughout the year, according to announcements made on its official website.

Applicants must complete the online application using the prescribed format and provide the required supporting materials.

Required Application Materials

Applicants must submit:

1. Two Recommendation Letters

Candidates must provide recommendation letters from two referees.

Applicants should therefore identify appropriate referees who can provide meaningful assessments of their academic and research capabilities.

2. Academic and Research Credentials

Applicants must provide copies of their relevant:

  • Academic credentials
  • Research credentials
  • Supporting evidence of their research achievements

These documents allow the selection committee to assess the candidate’s academic and research background.

3. Statement of Purpose

Applicants must submit a Statement of Purpose of at least 500 words.

The Statement of Purpose should provide an opportunity for applicants to explain their academic and research background, their research interests and their motivation for pursuing the post-doctoral fellowship.

Because the selection committee considers the applicant’s proposed research area, candidates should ensure that their application presents a clear and coherent research direction.

MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship Selection Process

After applications are submitted, they are reviewed and evaluated by a designated MUJ PDF Selection Committee.

The committee evaluates candidates based on several factors, including:

  • Academic credentials
  • Research credentials
  • Publication record
  • Proposed research area

Candidates who successfully pass the initial review may be shortlisted for an interview.

Monthly Interview Schedule

Shortlisted candidates will be invited for an interview.

The interviews are conducted once a month during the first week, subject to the availability of expert panel members.

This means applicants should be prepared for an interview as part of the selection process rather than expecting selection to be based solely on their written application.

Who Is on the MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship Selection Committee?

The fellowship guidelines specify the composition of the selection committee.

The committee includes:

  • Pro President — Chairperson
  • Dean RIAA
  • Concerned Academic Dean
  • Concerned Associate Dean
  • Concerned Heads of Department (HoDs)
  • Prospective Supervisors
  • Director Research — Member Secretary

The involvement of academic leaders, department representatives, prospective supervisors and research leadership means that candidates are evaluated from both academic and research perspectives.

Successful applicants will receive a formal letter of award from MUJ.

Research Supervision and Progress Monitoring

Each Post-Doctoral Fellow will be assigned a supervisor.

The supervisor will monitor:

  • Research progress
  • Administrative compliance

The supervision arrangement is intended to ensure that fellows remain on track with their research objectives while also meeting the administrative requirements associated with the fellowship.

Quarterly Progress Reports

Fellows are required to submit a quarterly progress report to their supervisor.

These reports should outline the research activities undertaken during the relevant period.

The process involves several levels of review:

  1. The fellow prepares and submits the quarterly progress report.
  2. The supervisor reviews the research progress.
  3. The Head of Department provides feedback.
  4. The reports and feedback are submitted to the Directorate of Research (DoR).
  5. The Directorate of Research evaluates the progress.

This reporting structure creates a formal mechanism for monitoring research performance throughout the fellowship.

Expected Research Outcomes

The fellowship has a clear publication expectation.

By the end of the fellowship, fellows are expected to publish or have accepted at least two research papers in Q1/Q2 journals.

This requirement reinforces the program’s emphasis on high-quality research output and aligns with the requirement that applicants already demonstrate a strong publication record before entering the fellowship.

Prospective applicants should therefore consider whether their proposed research can realistically generate high-quality scholarly outputs within the fellowship period.

Intellectual Property and Research Outputs

An important condition of the fellowship concerns ownership and affiliation of research outcomes.

The guidelines state that outcomes such as:

  • Research findings
  • Publications
  • Monographs
  • Patents
  • Other research outputs

must be affiliated with and remain the intellectual property of MUJ.

Applicants should understand this requirement before accepting the fellowship, particularly if their proposed research is likely to generate intellectual property, commercialisable research, patents or other valuable outputs.

Technology Transfer Opportunities

Where relevant, fellows are also expected to explore opportunities for technology transfer.

This is particularly relevant for research that could have practical, technological or commercial applications.

The requirement encourages fellows to consider how research findings and innovations might potentially move beyond academic publication toward practical implementation or broader use.

Is There an Application Deadline?

The MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship guidelines state that applications are invited throughout the year, as announced on the University’s official website.

Therefore, the provided fellowship information does not specify one fixed annual application deadline.

Deadline: Applications are accepted throughout the year, subject to announcements by MUJ.

Applicants should nevertheless monitor the official MUJ website for current calls and application instructions.

Why Researchers Should Consider the MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship

The fellowship offers several features that may appeal to early-career researchers who have already established a strong research profile.

The combination of a monthly stipend, research-related contingency funding, academic supervision and opportunities for high-quality publication makes the fellowship particularly relevant to researchers seeking to strengthen their post-doctoral research careers.

The opportunity can potentially help fellows:

  • Continue advanced research after completing a PhD
  • Develop an independent research profile
  • Produce additional Q1/Q2 journal publications
  • Participate in professional conferences
  • Present research findings
  • Cover eligible publication costs
  • Obtain research consumables and equipment
  • Work with an academic supervisor
  • Build connections within an academic department
  • Explore technology-transfer opportunities
  • Gain further academic experience through possible teaching and learning responsibilities

Key Requirements Applicants Should Check Before Applying

Before submitting an application, prospective candidates should confirm that they satisfy the major conditions:

  1. You are under 35 years old when you submit the application.
  2. You hold a PhD from a recognized institution in India or abroad.
  3. You have at least four Q1/Q2 journal papers published during the previous two years.
  4. If you earned your PhD from MUJ, you have completed at least one year of relevant post-PhD experience outside MUJ.
  5. You will not receive another external grant, financial aid or research assistance during the fellowship.
  6. You will not undertake part-time or full-time employment, including honorary employment, throughout the fellowship.
  7. You are prepared to submit two recommendation letters.
  8. You can provide your academic and research credentials.
  9. You can prepare a Statement of Purpose of at least 500 words.
  10. You are prepared to participate in the interview process if shortlisted.
  11. You understand the quarterly progress-reporting requirements.
  12. You are prepared to work toward the expected minimum of two Q1/Q2 publications by the end of the fellowship.

How to Prepare a Strong MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship Application

Applicants can improve their preparation by approaching the application as a research-focused academic opportunity rather than simply another post-doctoral position.

Develop a Clear Research Direction

Your proposed research area is one of the factors considered by the selection committee. Make sure your research direction is clearly articulated and demonstrates a meaningful academic purpose.

Highlight Your Recent Publications

Because the fellowship requires at least four Q1/Q2 papers from the last two years, applicants should clearly document their recent publication record.

Prepare Strong Recommendations

Choose referees who are familiar with your research and can provide credible assessments of your academic and research achievements.

Write a Strong Statement of Purpose

The Statement of Purpose must contain at least 500 words. It should be carefully prepared and should clearly communicate your research background, academic motivation and proposed direction.

Prepare for the Interview

Shortlisted applicants are invited to an interview, so candidates should be prepared to discuss their research credentials, publication record and proposed research area.

Understand the Fellowship Restrictions

Applicants should carefully consider the restrictions on external funding and employment before applying. Successful fellows cannot receive other external grants, financial aid or research assistance and cannot undertake part-time or full-time employment during the fellowship.

MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship at a Glance

Feature Details
Opportunity MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship
Institution MUJ
Nationality All nationalities
Age Under 35 at application
Academic requirement PhD from a recognized institution
Publication requirement At least 4 Q1/Q2 papers in the last 2 years
Monthly stipend ₹70,000
Contingency Grant I ₹50,000 per year
Contingency Grant II ₹50,000 per year
Initial duration 1 year
Possible extension Additional 1 year based on satisfactory performance
Application frequency Throughout the year
Statement of Purpose Minimum 500 words
Recommendation letters 2
Selection Application review and interview
Interview timing Once a month during the first week, subject to panel availability
Progress reporting Quarterly
Expected publication outcome At least 2 Q1/Q2 papers published or accepted by fellowship completion
Employment restriction No part-time or full-time employment during fellowship
Other funding restriction No external grants, financial aid or research assistance during fellowship

Conclusion

The MUJ Post-Doctoral Fellowship is a research-focused opportunity designed to attract high-performing young scholars from India and around the world. With a ₹70,000 monthly stipend, two annual contingency grants of ₹50,000 each, dedicated supervision and the possibility of a one-year extension, the program provides substantial support for researchers seeking to advance their academic careers.

However, the fellowship is aimed at candidates who have already demonstrated a strong record of research achievement. Applicants must be under 35, hold a recognized PhD and have published at least four Q1/Q2 papers within the previous two years. They must also be prepared to meet the fellowship’s restrictions concerning external financial support and employment.

Successful fellows will be expected to maintain regular research progress, submit quarterly reports and work toward producing at least two additional Q1/Q2 journal publications by the end of the fellowship. Research outputs will remain affiliated with and be the intellectual property of MUJ, while fellows may also be expected to explore technology-transfer opportunities where relevant.

With applications invited throughout the year, eligible researchers should monitor MUJ’s official announcements and prepare their academic credentials, publication evidence, recommendation letters, research plans and 500-word minimum Statement of Purpose in advance.

item.content:encoded:
Key Details: Cambridge Mastercard Foundation Scholarship 2027/2028

Scholarship Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program
University University of Cambridge
Academic year 2027/2028
Study level Master’s degree
Duration One-year full-time postgraduate courses
Eligible applicants Citizens of African countries
Main themes Climate resilience and sustainability
Tuition Full tuition costs covered
Living support Monthly maintenance allowance
Application Integrated into the Cambridge postgraduate application
Women encouraged to apply? Yes
Refugees encouraged to apply? Yes
Internally displaced people encouraged to apply? Yes
People with disabilities encouraged to apply? Yes

Applications for the 2027/2028 Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Cambridge are now open. The prestigious scholarship provides talented young Africans with the opportunity to pursue a fully funded one-year master’s degree at the University of Cambridge while developing their leadership potential and preparing to contribute to sustainable development in Africa.

The programme is designed for ambitious young Africans who are committed to creating positive change, particularly in the areas of climate resilience and sustainability.

Successful scholars receive comprehensive financial support designed to help them thrive during their studies at Cambridge, including full tuition fees and a monthly maintenance allowance.

Programme themes and eligibility

Our programme themes are climate resilience and sustainability. Recognising the wide range of expertise required to address these complex challenges, prospective Mastercard Foundation Scholars can apply for any full-time one-year postgraduate courses at the University, excluding:

  • Master of Business Administration (MBA)
  • Master of Corporate Law (MCL)
  • Master of Finance (MFIN)
  • Master of Accountancy (MACC)

To be eligible, you must:

  • Be a citizen of an African country.
  • Be resident in an African country, unless you can show temporary absence for study or work (exception – if you identify as an internally displaced person or have refugee status).
  • Meet the academic requirement of the course you’re applying for.

 

Eligibility

To be eligible for the programme, you must:

1. Have a bachelor’s degree.

2. Meet the academic entry requirements of your chosen course. Some courses require the equivalent of a UK first-class honours degree and others an upper second-class degree. Please use the postgraduate study course directory to check your course’s entry requirements.

3. Be from, and live in, an African country. You can apply if you’re temporarily living outside of Africa for study or work.

4. Apply for an eligible course. This can be any full-time master’s excluding:

  • Master of Accountancy (MACC)
  • Business Administration (MBA)
  • Master of Corporate Law (MCL)
  • Master of Finance (MFIN)

5. Demonstrate a commitment to giving back to your community, home country or Africa more generally, and to the themes of sustainability and climate resilience.

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion in higher education. Women, refugees, internally displaced persons, and people with disabilities are particularly encouraged to apply.

How to apply

Before getting started

☑️ Use the postgraduate course directory to find the course you want to apply for, then check its entry requirements, funding deadline and the supporting documents you’ll need: www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/courses

☑️ Navigate to the ‘Requirements’ tab and click on the link to check if the degree you currently hold meets Cambridge’s postgraduate academic entry requirements using the international qualifications checker.

1. Start your course application

Open your chosen course’s profile in the postgraduate course directory and click ‘Apply Now’. Create an account to save and return to your application later.

2. Apply for an application fee waiver (if required to do so)

Once you’ve opened your application, you can apply for an application fee waiver.

All Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program applicants are eligible for the application fee waiver if you meet the academic entry requirements of your chosen course.

If your country is listed below, the application fee will be waived automatically when you submit your application – you do not need to take any action.

Angola, Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Congo (Dem. Rep.), Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Mozambique, Niger, Rwanda, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania (United Rep. of), Togo, Uganda, and Zambia.

If your country does not appear on this list, you must submit an application fee request form using the link below, attaching copies of your transcript and passport:

Application Fee Waiver Form

Please complete the form as early as possible, and by the deadline of 18 November 2026.

3. Apply for funding

During your application, opt in for funding to view eligible options. If you meet your chosen course’s entry requirements, you’ll be able to select the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program.

Write your scholarship statement, focusing on:

  • Your career / education history
  • Leadership potential
  • How the scholarship will help you achieve your goals and aspirations
  • How you hope to contribute to sustainable futures in Africa

4. Complete and submit your application

Submit your application by the course’s funding deadline – usually early December or January, earlier than the standard deadline.

You’ll also be asked to choose a College. This is where you’ll live, eat and have small group teaching sessions. Find out about the University’s 31 Colleges and how to choose one.

5. Departments select successful applicants

Departments select applicants on a rolling basis, with offers made between December and February. Selection is based on your course application and not your scholarship statement.

Some departments interview shortlisted candidates before making an offer.

6. Selection for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program

The team reviews applicants who have been offered a place on their chosen course and selects scholars based on both the course application and scholarship statement.

Offer letters are sent in late March or early April.

7. Submit any outstanding documents

If successful, submit any outstanding documents by 31 July. This will usually include IELTS test results. The score required by most courses is either 7.0 or 7.5 overall but it’s important to check your course’s language requirements.

(You can apply without IELTS results. If your application is successful, you’ll receive a conditional offer).

Application process timeline

Stage Date
Applications open Early September
Application and Funding deadline Depending on your course – either early December or early January
Departmental selection December – February
Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program selection Late February / Early March
Scholarships offered March / April

Find out more

We’re holding a series of webinars during the application period – an opportunity to find out more about the programme and how to apply.

  • Tuesday 22 September, 11am (UK): Sign up now
  • Tuesday 6 October, 11am (UK): Sign up now

More sessions to be added

The programme supports diversity in all its forms and actively encourages women, refugees, internally displaced people, and people with disabilities to apply.

FAQ

Which courses are eligible for funding?

In recognition of the wide range of expertise needed to drive sustainable change, you can apply for most full-time master’s courses available. The only exceptions are:

  • Master of Accountancy (MACC)
  • Business Administration (MBA)
  • Master of Corporate Law (MCL)
  • Master of Finance (MFIN)

Courses will vary in length from 9 – 12 months – that’s fine as long as they’re full-time.

How can I get support with my application?

The university is running a series of information sessions during the application window – an opportunity to look at the application process in detail and ask the team questions. Please keep an eye on the news section of this website and our LinkedIn for details.

For questions, please contact admin@mastercardfoundation.fund.cam.ac.uk.

Please note – we have been made aware of a scam where applicants are offered support with their application from someone claiming to be associated with the University of Cambridge in return for payment. You should not pay anyone for support with your application.

What are the academic entry requirements?

Academic entry requirements differ depending by course. Please check the requirements for your chosen course using the postgraduate course directory before you apply (Course Directory | Postgraduate Study).

Many courses require a first-class degree. Some an upper second.

Is there an age limit?

There is no upper age limit for the Mastercard Foundation Scholar Program in Cambridge.

What does the scholarship cover?

The university aim to cover everything you need to pursue your master’s and get the most out of your time in Cambridge, including:

  • Course fee
  • Maintenance / living allowance
  • Visa and health surcharge
  • Travel inc. flights and taxi into Cambridge
  • Laptop

Will I receive an application fee waiver for more than one course?

No, you will receive an application fee waiver for one course. We recommend thinking carefully about the course you’re best suited to and focus on making that application as strong as possible.

When is the deadline?

The deadline differs by course but is generally either the first week of December or the first week of January.

Please note: it’s the funding deadline you need to work towards which will be earlier than the standard course application deadline listed. If not listed or unclear, please get in touch with your department and ask.

Is the funding transferable to the next year if I’m unable to take up my place?

No, the scholarship offer is subject to you meeting all other University conditions set for the year of application. It cannot be transferred to the following year.

What’s the College system and how do I choose one?

Cambridge is collegiate university, meaning you’ll be a member of one of 31 colleges.
Colleges are responsible for admitting students, providing accommodation, and for pastoral care.

Your college will be your home away from home, and you’ll be a part of a community of students studying a variety of subjects. Some of the other advantages of college membership include induction in your first weeks, financial advice and assistance, and opportunities for research, teaching, and professional development.

Colleges administer formal processes, including matriculation (formally joining the University and College), monitoring international students’ status for visa purposes, and graduation.

All colleges have their own websites you can look at and you can take You can take virtual tours of many colleges too.

www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/colleges
www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/colleges/college-listing

When will I hear back regarding my application for funding?

Scholarship offer letters are sent in April.

How long will I have to confirm acceptance of the funding offer?

This will be covered in your offer letter. Normally 10 working days from the date the offer was made.

Can you cover travel expenses for my spouse or children?

As of January 2024, the UK Home Office stopped allowing students on one-year master’s programmes to bring their spouse and/or children on their visa. This means we cannot support travel expenses for a spouse or child.

On arrival how do I get from the airport to Cambridge?

We arrange transport from the airport to Cambridge and will share a logistics note with details of transfers before you travel.

Where can I get extra support as an African student coming to Cambridge?

The African Society of Cambridge University (ASCU), a body run by African students, offers help, support and a community away from home.

You can also access support through the University’s Newcomers and Visiting Scholars group.

Can I apply if my undergraduate degree is from a country outside of Africa?

Yes, as long as you’re resident in Africa or you’re currently away studying.

Can you apply if you’re a dual African / UK passport holder?

No.

Can I apply for PhD funding?

Not from the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program in Cambridge.

We suggest using the postgraduate funding search on the student funding website. You’ll find several opportunities including the Cambridge Trust Changemakers Scholarship and the Gates Cambridge and Harding PhD scholarships.

Search – Postgraduate Funding Search

Source: https://www.mastercardfoundation.fund.cam.ac.uk/news/2027-applications-now-open

item.content:encoded:
Grassroots organisations working to address pressing social challenges in their local communities can apply for funding through the Comic Relief Community Fund (England) 2026/27. Delivered by Groundwork in partnership with Comic Relief, the programme is designed to provide financial support to community-led organisations that are creating positive change and improving the lives of people in their communities.

For the 2026/27 funding round, grants of up to £5,000 will be awarded to organisations in England. The programme has a particular focus on initiatives addressing homelessness and the cost of living, early childhood development, violence against women and girls, and the safety and wellbeing of refugees, asylum seekers and people experiencing forced migration.

With a total funding allocation of just over £600,000, the programme expects to support approximately 120 organisations across England.

What Is the Comic Relief Community Fund?

The Comic Relief Community Fund is a grant programme supporting grassroots and community-led organisations that are working to make a meaningful difference in their local communities.

Groundwork has partnered with Comic Relief to deliver the programme in England since 2019. The initiative recognises that smaller, locally rooted organisations often have a strong understanding of the challenges faced by their communities because they work directly with people experiencing those challenges.

The fund therefore seeks to support organisations that draw on the lived experience of the people and communities they serve when developing and delivering their work.

For the 2026/27 programme, funding will be directed towards organisations undertaking projects that respond to some of the most significant social and economic challenges affecting communities in England.

Comic Relief Community Fund 2026/27 Key Details

Applicants should take note of the following important information:

  • Funding amount: Grants of up to £5,000
  • Total funding available: Just over £600,000
  • Expected number of organisations supported: Approximately 120
  • Location: England
  • Application opening date: Tuesday, 1 September 2026
  • Application deadline: 5pm on Wednesday, 30 September 2026
  • Project completion deadline: All funded projects must be delivered by 30 September 2027
  • Eligible costs: Funding can support project costs, core organisational costs, or a combination of both
  • Geographical requirement: Organisations must be located in the same region in which their funded projects will be delivered
  • Previous grant recipients: Organisations receiving a 2025/26 grant may apply for the new funding round provided their previous project is completed and the required end-of-grant report has been submitted by 30 September 2026

Applicants are encouraged to review the full programme criteria and application guidance before submitting an application.

How Much Funding Is Available?

Successful organisations can receive a grant of up to £5,000.

Although the individual grant size is relatively small, the funding is intended to provide flexible support to grassroots organisations that may have limited access to larger funding opportunities.

The programme has a total allocation of just over £600,000, with approximately 120 organisations expected to receive funding.

The funding can be particularly useful for community organisations seeking to:

  • Launch a new local project.
  • Expand an existing community initiative.
  • Respond to an emerging need within their community.
  • Cover eligible core organisational costs.
  • Strengthen the delivery of an existing programme.
  • Combine organisational and project-related expenditure.
  • Support activities designed around the needs and experiences of local beneficiaries.

What Will the Comic Relief Community Fund Support?

The 2026/27 programme has identified several priority areas. Organisations should ensure that their proposed activities clearly demonstrate how they respond to the needs addressed by the fund.

1. Tackling Homelessness

One of the major priorities of the 2026/27 programme is tackling homelessness.

Funding may therefore be relevant to grassroots organisations working with people who are homeless, at risk of homelessness, or experiencing barriers to secure and stable housing.

Community-led organisations addressing homelessness may be involved in initiatives that respond to local needs and help vulnerable people access appropriate support, improve their circumstances or strengthen their connection with community services.

2. Addressing Cost-of-Living Concerns

The fund also focuses on initiatives supporting people experiencing cost-of-living concerns.

Rising household costs can place significant pressure on individuals and families, particularly those already experiencing financial insecurity or other forms of disadvantage.

Grassroots organisations with initiatives designed to help communities cope with cost-of-living challenges may therefore find this funding opportunity relevant to their work.

Projects should demonstrate an understanding of the challenges facing the communities they serve and explain how the proposed activities can contribute to positive local change.

3. Supporting Early Childhood Development

Another priority area is early childhood development.

The programme recognises the importance of supporting children during the early stages of life and initiatives that contribute to positive childhood development may be considered within the fund’s priorities.

Community organisations working with children, families and caregivers can consider whether their existing or proposed activities align with this focus.

Projects should demonstrate a clear connection between the proposed activities and the needs of the children, families or communities they seek to support.

4. Preventing Violence Against Women and Girls

The 2026/27 fund also prioritises projects supporting the prevention of violence against women and girls.

This provides an opportunity for grassroots organisations working to improve safety, awareness, prevention, community support and related areas to seek financial assistance for eligible activities.

Organisations should clearly explain the problem they are addressing, the communities affected and how their proposed work can contribute to preventing violence or improving safety and support.

5. Supporting Refugees and Asylum Seekers

The fund includes initiatives that support the safety of refugees and asylum seekers.

Organisations working directly with refugee and asylum-seeking communities may therefore consider whether their activities meet the programme’s criteria.

This could be particularly relevant to community-led organisations with strong local relationships and an understanding of the challenges faced by refugees and asylum seekers.

6. Supporting People Experiencing Forced Migration

The programme also recognises the needs of people experiencing forced migration.

Grassroots organisations supporting people affected by displacement and forced migration can explore the programme criteria to determine whether their proposed activities qualify for funding.

A strong application should demonstrate how the organisation’s work responds to locally identified needs and how the project can create meaningful benefits for the people it supports.

What Can the Grant Funding Be Used For?

One of the important features of the Comic Relief Community Fund is the flexibility around eligible expenditure.

Funding can be used for:

  • Project costs
  • Core organisational costs
  • A combination of project and core organisational costs

This flexibility can be particularly valuable for grassroots organisations because smaller community organisations may require support not only for individual activities but also for the organisational capacity needed to deliver those activities effectively.

Applicants should nevertheless consult the official application guidance to understand the specific costs and activities permitted under the programme.

Who Can Apply?

The Comic Relief Community Fund is intended for grassroots, community-led organisations based in England that are working to create positive change within their local communities.

The programme places importance on organisations that understand the needs of their communities and draw on the lived experience of the people they support.

An organisation considering applying should carefully assess the full eligibility requirements contained in the official application guidance before preparing its application.

Geographic Eligibility

The 2026/27 programme is specifically for organisations in England.

An important requirement is that an organisation must be located in the same region where the funded project will be delivered.

This means organisations should pay close attention to the geographic relationship between their own location and the location of their proposed activities.

The opportunity is therefore not a general international grant programme. Organisations based outside England should not assume that they are eligible simply because their work addresses one of the programme’s priority areas.

Organisational Size and Grassroots Focus

Groundwork has worked with Comic Relief since 2019 as an intermediary funder supporting grassroots community organisations in England, particularly organisations with a turnover of under £250,000.

Applicants should check the current application guidance to confirm the precise eligibility requirements for the 2026/27 funding round rather than relying solely on previous programme information.

The grassroots focus is important because the fund is designed to reach organisations that are closely connected to the communities they serve.

Can Previous Comic Relief Community Fund Recipients Apply?

Yes, organisations that received a 2025/26 grant can apply to the new 2026/27 fund.

However, there is an important condition.

Their previous project must have been completed and the required end-of-grant report submitted by Wednesday, 30 September 2026.

Organisations that received previous funding should therefore ensure that they have completed all reporting requirements before applying for the new funding round.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Although receiving a grant is not guaranteed, applicants can improve the quality of their submissions by clearly demonstrating the relevance and impact of their proposed work.

1. Clearly Identify the Community Need

Start by explaining the issue your organisation is addressing.

A strong application should make it easy for the funder to understand:

  • What problem exists?
  • Who is affected?
  • Where does the problem occur?
  • Why is the issue important?
  • What evidence or lived experience demonstrates the need?
  • Why is your organisation well positioned to respond?

2. Connect Your Project to a Priority Area

Your proposal should clearly demonstrate how it relates to one or more of the fund’s 2026/27 priorities.

These include:

  • Homelessness
  • Cost-of-living concerns
  • Early childhood development
  • Prevention of violence against women and girls
  • Safety of refugees and asylum seekers
  • Support for people experiencing forced migration

Avoid presenting a project without clearly explaining its connection to the programme’s priorities.

3. Demonstrate Community Involvement

The programme places emphasis on community-led approaches and lived experience.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate how the people they support have influenced the organisation’s understanding of the issue and, where relevant, the design and delivery of the proposed project.

4. Explain How the Money Will Be Used

Because grants are limited to a maximum of £5,000, applicants should present a realistic and clearly structured budget.

Explain how the requested funding will contribute to the proposed activities and how each major cost supports the project’s objectives.

5. Demonstrate Local Impact

Applicants should explain the expected benefits of the project for the local community.

Consider describing:

  • Who will benefit.
  • How many people may benefit.
  • What activities will be delivered.
  • What changes the project is expected to achieve.
  • How the organisation will know whether the project has made a difference.

6. Check the Eligibility Criteria Carefully

Before submitting an application, organisations should read the full programme criteria and application guidance.

This is especially important because the fund has specific requirements relating to organisational location, project delivery, previous grants and other eligibility considerations.

Previous Impact of the Comic Relief and Groundwork Partnership

The partnership between Groundwork and Comic Relief has been operating since 2019.

According to the programme information, the partnership has so far achieved significant reach across communities in England.

The programme reports:

  • £6.3 million in grant funding awarded.
  • 1,462 grants awarded.
  • Approximately 156,000 beneficiaries supported.
  • Around 3,000 volunteering opportunities created.

These figures illustrate the scale of the partnership’s support for grassroots organisations and the communities they serve.

Important Deadline for the Comic Relief Community Fund 2026/27

The application window opens on:

Tuesday, 1 September 2026

The deadline for applications is:

5pm on Wednesday, 30 September 2026

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their applications. Organisations should allow sufficient time to review the eligibility criteria, prepare their project information, develop a realistic budget and check the application before submission.

All successful projects must be delivered by:

30 September 2027

Organisations that received a 2025/26 grant and intend to apply for the new funding round must also ensure that their previous project has been completed and the end-of-grant report submitted by 30 September 2026.

How to Apply for the Comic Relief Community Fund

Organisations interested in applying should visit the official Groundwork Comic Relief Community Fund website and access the How to Apply section.

The application guidance provides the detailed programme criteria that applicants need to understand before submitting their proposals.

Applicants should use the official guidance as the authoritative source for determining eligibility, eligible expenditure, application requirements and other conditions.

About Groundwork and Comic Relief

The Comic Relief Community Fund in England is delivered through a partnership between Comic Relief and Groundwork.

Groundwork acts as an intermediary funder, supporting grassroots community organisations and helping channel funding towards locally driven initiatives.

Comic Relief is known for supporting projects and organisations working to tackle social challenges and improve people’s lives, while Groundwork works with communities to create positive environmental, social and economic change.

Their continued partnership provides a mechanism for directing funding towards community organisations that are often deeply embedded within the communities they serve.

Why This Funding Opportunity Matters

Small grants can play an important role in helping grassroots organisations turn community ideas into practical action.

For smaller organisations, even a grant of £5,000 can provide resources for activities that might otherwise be difficult to implement.

The flexibility to use funding towards project costs, core organisational costs or a combination of both can also help organisations strengthen their ability to deliver community-focused initiatives.

The 2026/27 priorities are particularly relevant to organisations responding to issues such as homelessness, financial hardship, child development, gender-based violence, displacement and migration.

By directing funding towards community-led organisations, the programme aims to support initiatives that are grounded in local realities and informed by the experiences of the people who benefit from them.

Visit HERE for more information about the Comic Relief Community Fund 2026/27.

Key Takeaways

The most important points for prospective applicants are

  1. The Comic Relief Community Fund 2026/27 is a funding opportunity for grassroots and community-led organisations in England.
  2. Grants of up to £5,000 are available.
  3. More than £600,000 in total funding is expected to be distributed.
  4. Approximately 120 organisations are expected to receive grants.
  5. The programme focuses on homelessness, cost-of-living concerns, early childhood development, violence against women and girls, and support for refugees, asylum seekers and people experiencing forced migration.
  6. Funding may be used for project costs, core organisational costs, or a combination of both.
  7. Organisations must be located in the same region where their funded projects will be delivered.
  8. Organisations receiving a 2025/26 grant may apply provided their previous project is completed and the end-of-grant report submitted by 30 September 2026.
  9. Applications close at 5pm on Wednesday, 30 September 2026.
  10. Funded projects must be completed by 30 September 2027.
  11. Applicants should consult the full programme criteria and application guidance before applying.

Conclusion

The Comic Relief Community Fund 2026/27 provides an important funding opportunity for grassroots organisations in England that are working directly with communities to address pressing social challenges.

With grants of up to £5,000, the programme can help locally rooted organisations develop or strengthen initiatives addressing homelessness, cost-of-living pressures, early childhood development, violence against women and girls, and the safety and wellbeing of refugees, asylum seekers and people experiencing forced migration.

The programme’s emphasis on community-led action and lived experience makes it particularly relevant to organisations that have a strong understanding of the challenges facing the people they support.

Eligible organisations should carefully review the official criteria, prepare a clear proposal demonstrating local need and expected impact, develop a realistic budget and submit their application before the 5pm, 30 September 2026 deadline.

For complete eligibility requirements, application guidance and submission instructions, applicants should consult the official Comic Relief Community Fund information provided by Groundwork.
